options: Function declaration (prototype) on line 1 satisfies the forward reference; definition on line 3 provides the implementation
C allows calling undefined functions
The compiler automatically generates a default func() if none exists
Compiler error: func is used before definition
explanation: A function prototype (declaration) without a body is a forward declaration; the actual definition can come later in the file.

options: Old C (no prototypes): the call is uncheck, assumes the prototype exists; modern C with -std=c99+ and warnings would flag this
C automatically fills missing arguments with 0
Compiler error: missing argument
The second argument defaults to b=0
explanation: Without a full prototype visible at the call site (K&R style), the compiler cannot verify argument count; calling with too few arguments is unpredictable.

options: The first return exits the function; code after return is unreachable
Both returns execute sequentially
Compiler error: duplicate return
The second return overrides the first
explanation: A return statement immediately transfers control out of the function; subsequent statements are unreachable.

options: void in the parameter list explicitly forbids arguments; func(42) violates this
func only accepts one argument: 42
Compiler allows extra arguments to be ignored
The function signature is ignored at call time
explanation: void parameters mean the function takes no arguments; passing any argument is a type error.

options: x is a local variable; its storage is destroyed when func returns; the pointer points to deallocated memory
Returning pointers from functions is not allowed
The address of a local variable is always invalid
Compiler error: cannot return address of local
explanation: Local variables are stack-allocated; when the function returns, their memory is reused; the returned pointer becomes a dangling pointer.

options: To allow variadic arguments (variable number of arguments) after the fixed parameters
To denote the end of the function declaration
To indicate optional parameters
Compiler error: ... is invalid syntax
explanation: The ... (ellipsis) enables variadic functions; va_start/va_arg macros allow accessing the variable arguments.

options: Exponential time complexity: same subproblems are recalculated repeatedly; fibonacci(n-2) is computed many times
Recursion is inherently slower than loops
The function does not use memoization
Integer overflow prevents computing large values
explanation: Naive recursive fibonacci has O(2^n) time; dynamic programming or memoization reduces this to O(n).

options: Stack space depends on platform/OS; a recursive depth limit is unreliable for detecting actual stack exhaustion
The counter always prevents overflow
Stack overflow cannot be detected in C
printf() itself causes stack overflow
explanation: Stack size varies; the depth counter is heuristic, not deterministic; the function could overflow at any depth or avoid it.

question:
static int func() { return 1; }
Can this function be called from other files?
options: No: static limits linkage to this translation unit only
Yes: static is a style convention with no effect on linkage
Only if the function is declared extern in the other file
Compiler error: static functions must be exported
explanation: static on a function restricts its linkage to internal (file-scope); other translation units cannot call it.
